paper_metadata.title: Achieving superior high-temperature strength in an additively manufactured high-entropy alloy by controlled heat treatment

evidence.quote: a high-strength HEA, (CoCrNi)94(TiAl)6, is selected and subjected to laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) and ageing treatment.

evidence.quote: At room temperature, the sample deforms mainly by dislocation slip and formation of stacking faults while at elevated temperatures, deformation becomes increasingly planar as characterized by the formation of increased number of stacking faults and the activation of twinning.

The higher EL in the samples made with 175 W-60 μs may be due to the absence of lack-of-fusion pores which should have delayed failure (Supplementary Fig. 3a-c). This is possible because lack-of-fusion pores are well known to be extremely harmful for ductility [63,64].
